With Kamala Harris' Vice President, do you believe this reflects a changing political landscape in the United States with more women of colour finally breaking through the glass ceiling? Or do you feel disappointment was more about taking the right boxes?

So when I got to Congress, the freshman class that won the 2018 election was the most diverse in race, in faith, in ethnicity, and in age. And I think a lot of people saw huge potential in the American people because it was a complete rejection of everything that Trump and his party was pushing our country towards. And I think with the last presidential election, with having Vice President Harris on the ticket, I think it inspired a lot of people, again, in the same way that not even our election, but even prior to that, with Obama's campaign and election, was inspiring. What's disheartening is that we are seeing a similar trend to what happened when Obama was elected. There was a lot of people who were hopeful with the hope and change message that voted, but then there was a huge backlash. It's something that is alarming to a lot of people when they hear about the amount of debt an average student has in the United States which It stays with you until you die unless you pay it off. There are members of Congress even who have, you know, somewhere between 150 to $250,000 in student debt. These are not people who went to become a doctor, they went to school to become teachers. And so these are not professions that pay you enough to be able to pay back that kind of student debt. And for me, it's an important one I carry student debt.
